title: Alkenes
keyIdea: Alkenes are hydrocarbons with one carbon–carbon double bond, C=C. Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ: ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆, butene C₄H₈. Because the double bond can open and take on more atoms, alkenes are unsaturated, and they turn orange bromine water colourless.

kid: Alkenes are a family of hydrocarbons. That means they are made of only carbon and hydrogen. Every alkene has two carbons joined by a double bond, written C=C.
A carbon atom always makes four bonds. The double bond uses up two of them. So the two carbons in the C=C each have room for one hydrogen less than in an alkane.
The smallest alkene is ethene, C₂H₄. Next come propene, C₃H₆, and butene, C₄H₈. Look at the numbers. There are always twice as many hydrogens as carbons.

Alkenes are called unsaturated. The double bond can open up and grab more atoms. You can test for this with orange bromine water. Shake it with an alkene and the colour vanishes. With an alkane it stays orange.
adult: An alkene is a hydrocarbon containing one carbon–carbon double bond. The names end in -ene: ethene, propene, butene, pentene. Each name uses the same stem as the alkane with the same number of carbons.

Carbon forms four bonds, and the C=C counts as two of them. Each carbon in the double bond therefore holds one hydrogen fewer than in the matching alkane. That makes two fewer in total, so the general formula is CₙH₂ₙ rather than CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Propene is CH₂=CH–CH₃.

Alkanes are saturated: every carbon already has four single bonds, so no more atoms can be added. Alkenes are unsaturated, because the C=C can open and bond to new atoms. With bromine, ethene forms C₂H₄Br₂. That addition removes the orange colour of bromine water, which is the standard test for a C=C.

Common mistakes: drawing three hydrogens on a C=C carbon, so each carbon has five bonds; removing only one hydrogen for the double bond; and reversing the bromine water test. Be careful too with ring compounds. A ring of carbons can also fit CₙH₂ₙ, so the formula alone suggests a chain alkene, but the drawing settles it.

familyTip: Use dried pasta for bonds and coins for atoms. Build ethane with single pasta bonds, then rebuild it as ethene with two pieces of pasta between the carbons. Count how many coin hydrogens you had to take away, and check every carbon still has four pieces of pasta.

worked.title: You are shown C₃H₈ and C₃H₆. Which is the alkene, and how is it drawn?
steps: Test each formula. For n = 3, an alkane has 2 × 3 + 2 = 8 hydrogens and an alkene has 2 × 3 = 6.
So C₃H₈ is propane, an alkane, and C₃H₆ is propene, the alkene.
Draw three carbons in a row and put a double bond between the first two: C=C–C.
Fill each carbon to four bonds: 2 H on the first carbon, 1 H on the middle one and 3 H on the last. That gives CH₂=CH–CH₃, six hydrogens in total.

practice.prompt: What makes a hydrocarbon an alkene?
choices: It has one carbon–carbon double bond
It contains oxygen as well as carbon
practice.hint: Look at the -ene ending and the bond between two carbons in ethene.
practice.explain: An alkene has a C=C double bond. Hydrocarbons with only single bonds are alkanes, and a hydrocarbon contains no oxygen.

practice.prompt: An alkene has {n} carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
practice.hint: Use CₙH₂ₙ: the number of hydrogens is twice the number of carbons.

practice.prompt: An alkene has {n} carbon atoms. Using C = 12 and H = 1, what is its relative formula mass?
practice.hint: Work out the formula with CₙH₂ₙ first, then add 12 for each C and 1 for each H.
practice.explain: The alkene is C{n}H{=2*n}: {n} × 12 + {=2*n} × 1 = {=14*n}. Each CH₂ adds 14.

practice.prompt: Which formula belongs to an alkene?
practice.hint: Check whether the number of hydrogens is exactly twice the number of carbons.
practice.explain: C₄H₈ fits CₙH₂ₙ, so it is butene. C₄H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, butane, and no stable hydrocarbon is C₄H₉.

practice.prompt: Why is ethene described as unsaturated?
choices: Its C=C bond can open and add more atoms
It does not dissolve in water
It has fewer carbon atoms than ethane
practice.hint: Saturated means full. What can happen to the double bond?
practice.explain: Unsaturated means more atoms can still be added. The C=C can open, for example adding bromine to make C₂H₄Br₂. Ethene and ethane both have 2 carbons.

pool.prompt: You are shown C₃H₈ and C₃H₆. Which one is an alkene?
pool.hint: For 3 carbons, an alkene has 2 × 3 hydrogens.
pool.explain: C₃H₆ fits CₙH₂ₙ, so it is propene. C₃H₈ fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so it is propane, an alkane.

pool.prompt: Which is the correct displayed structure of propene, written in short?
pool.hint: Every carbon needs exactly four bonds. The double bond counts as two.
pool.explain: In CH₂=CH–CH₃ each carbon has four bonds. CH₃= would give the first carbon five bonds, and =CH₂– would give the middle carbon five.

pool.prompt: Orange bromine water is shaken with a hydrocarbon and turns colourless. What does this show?
choices: The hydrocarbon has a C=C double bond
pool.hint: Which kind of hydrocarbon can add bromine atoms?
pool.explain: Bromine adds across a C=C, which removes its colour. Alkanes have no double bond, so they leave bromine water orange.

pool.prompt: An alkene has {=2*n} hydrogen atoms. How many carbon atoms does it have?
pool.hint: In CₙH₂ₙ the hydrogens are twice the carbons, so work backwards.

pool.prompt: A molecule of an alkene with {n} carbons reacts with bromine, Br₂. How many atoms does the product molecule contain in total?
pool.hint: Count the carbons and hydrogens of CₙH₂ₙ, then add the two bromine atoms that join across the C=C.
pool.explain: {n} C + {=2*n} H + 2 Br = {=3*n+2} atoms, for example C₂H₄Br₂ for ethene.

pool.prompt: In ethene, how many hydrogen atoms are bonded to each carbon?
pool.hint: Each carbon makes 4 bonds, and 2 of them are in the C=C.
pool.explain: 4 − 2 = 2, so each carbon holds 2 H: CH₂=CH₂, which is C₂H₄.

pool.prompt: Leo says alkanes are unsaturated because they have lots of hydrogen. What is wrong?
choices: Alkanes are saturated: every carbon already has four single bonds
Alkanes have no hydrogen at all
pool.hint: Saturated means no more atoms can be added. Can more be added to an alkane?
pool.explain: In an alkane every carbon already has four single bonds, so nothing more can add. That makes alkanes saturated, and alkenes unsaturated.

pool.prompt: Which name matches the alkene C₄H₈?
pool.hint: The stem gives the number of carbons and the ending tells you the family.
pool.explain: But- means 4 carbons and -ene means a C=C, so C₄H₈ is butene. Butane is C₄H₁₀ and propene is C₃H₆.

visual.caption: Alkene or alkane? Check whether the H count is 2 × C or 2 × C + 2. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: add the hydrogens to ethene, propene and butene, then test each molecule with bromine water.
